tweetHighlights.originalTitle: We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g.
tweetHighlights.originalBody:
We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g. "create an svg of pelican on a bicycle". As one idea to generalize it, I was interested what Opus 5 would do if I gave it the first paragraph of the Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (~$10) and asked for three js render of it. Opus went off for ~2 hours and wrote 5500 lines of code that (procedurally) rendered the story. It's kind of janky but fun. But it's a bit mindboggling that the LLM has to place and orchestrate various polygon assets in (x,y,z) coordinates and write code that animates it all, and that it even does anything at all.

I also like this kind of examples because no one in their right mind would ever spend the time to write something this custom but LLMs have all the stamina and patience in the world, so it's an example where we go from "no one would ever do this" to "sure, why not, it's ~free". There might be a lot more. But I'm excited about creating hyper custom worlds that you can imagine dropping players into, e.g. here to participate in the LoTR story as a spectator NPC, or one of the characters, or etc. Something like an ephemeral GTA of X on demand.

Last thought is that the domain of worlds/games exposes a weakness in LLMs: they can't easily audit their work because they aren't able to efficiently and natively perceive videos or play games within them. Here, Opus 5 had to very slowly and painstakingly take screenshots at different points, and it messed up a few times and created a bunch of jank. An example of raw capability (multimodal, gameplay) that I think is still quite lacking.
tweetHighlights.translatedTitle: 我们开始离开那种通过例如以下方式测试LLM的领域：
tweetHighlights.translatedBody:
我们现在开始偏离那种通过例如“创建一个骑自行车的鹈鹕的 SVG”来测试 LLM 的领域了。为了更全面地了解它，我很好奇如果我给 Opus 5 提供《指环王》的第一段文字、100 万代币预算（约 10 美元），并要求它渲染三个 JavaScript 版本，它会怎么做。Opus 运行了大约 2 个小时，编写了 5500 行代码（程序化地）渲染了这个故事。虽然有点粗糙，但很有趣。但 LLM 需要将各种多边形资源放置在 (x, y, z) 坐标系中并进行协调，还要编写代码来实现动画效果，而且它最终还能完成这些工作，这确实令人难以置信。

我也很喜欢这类例子，因为正常人根本不会花时间去写这么定制化的东西，但LLM（游戏开发者）却拥有无穷的精力和耐心，所以这说明我们的想法是从“没人会这么做”到“当然可以，反正也免费”。可能还有很多这样的例子。但我很兴奋能创造出高度定制化的世界，你可以想象把玩家放到其中，比如让他们以旁观NPC或角色的身份参与《指环王》的故事，等等。就像一个可以随时体验的限时版《侠盗猎车手》X。

最后一点是，世界/游戏领域暴露了LLM的一个弱点：他们无法轻松地审核自己的作品，因为他们无法高效地原生感知视频或在视频中玩游戏。比如，Opus 5不得不非常缓慢且费力地在不同的时间点截取屏幕截图，结果几次出错，导致画面出现了很多瑕疵。这是一个原始能力（多模式、游戏玩法）的例子，我认为它仍然相当不足。

tweetHighlights.originalBody:
We’re going to see an increasing divergence between what AI does in our personal lives and in daily productivity vs. what it can do in very deep domains like math, science, legal, coding and more.

Up to some threshold, capability was evenly felt across all domains because the models were just becoming mildly useful in general. Now, the deep domain work is about to go vertical. 

Most people won’t actually notice these benefits in their day to day life directly (indirectly they certainly will over time), but the experts in these fields will. And there’s no inherent ceiling to what capabilities are needed, unlike in the consumer space where needs can get met relatively straightforwardly.

This will often lead to a capability overhang, though, as many of these performance gains need to be applied to data sets and workflows in an applied way for that area of work. But this is ultimately how you get breakthroughs in life sciences, real world automation, new cyber capabilities, and more.
tweetHighlights.translatedTitle: 我们将看到人工智能在我们个人生活中所做的事情与人类行为之间的差异越来越大……
tweetHighlights.translatedBody:
我们将看到人工智能在个人生活和日常生产力方面的作用，与它在数学、科学、法律、编程等深奥领域所能发挥的作用之间，出现越来越大的差异。

在达到某个阈值之前，人工智能的能力在所有领域都得到了均衡的体现，因为这些模型在总体上才刚刚开始具备一定的实用性。如今，深奥领域的应用即将垂直化。

大多数人可能不会直接感受到这些益处（随着时间的推移，他们肯定会间接感受到），但这些领域的专家会。而且，与消费领域不同，深奥领域所需的能力没有固有的上限，消费领域的需求可以相对直接地得到满足。

然而，这往往会导致能力过剩，因为许多性能提升需要以应用的方式应用于特定领域的数据集和工作流程。但归根结底，这正是我们在生命科学、现实世界自动化、新型网络安全能力等领域取得突破的根本途径。

tweetHighlights.originalBody:
I'm feeling spicy tonight so let me just say it:

I think Opus 4.6 was the Opus model with the best personality and writing style.

Something's off with Opus 5 - it tends to give me overly long replies, use Claude-speak way too much (e.g., "here's the honest truth"), and is too judgemental. 

Opus used to be a joy to talk to like a trusted friend. Not so much anymore.

tweetHighlights.translatedBody:
今晚我心情不错，就直说了吧：

我觉得 Opus 4.6 是 Opus 系列里个性和写作风格最好的。

Opus 5 有点不对劲——它回复的内容总是太长，说话也太像克劳德（Claude）的风格（比如，“实话实说”），而且太爱评判别人了。

以前和 Opus 聊天就像和一位值得信赖的朋友聊天一样愉快。现在却不是这样了。

tweetHighlights.originalBody:
You should be able to pledge tokens for issues that you open and open source repos. 

Write a spec in the issue with a pledge. If the maintainer accepts, GitHub passes the issue verbatim to a cloud coding agent at the requester’s expense. 

No more slop PRs
